subject: Subprocessor continuity / upcoming retirements — action steps and evidence request
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marie Lopez <marie.lopez@blueharbor.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Subprocessor continuity / upcoming retirements — initial ask

Hi Marie —

Quick note: BlueHarbor flagged a potential problem if one of our telemetry subprocessors (EdgeSight) retires in January. Before we get to contractual changes, could you confirm whether BlueHarbor requires a formal replacement notice + 30-day review window for retirements, or if a 14-day notice plus continuity evidence is acceptable?

To help speed things along, I attached our latest roster and an initial impact matrix (attachment). If you need more detail about cross-border routes or KMS custody for EU tenants, let me know which tenants you want prioritized.

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm notice window required by BlueHarbor procurement/compliance
- We provide an impact matrix broken down by tenant/region and proposed onshore fallback
- Provide evidence: contract amendment template + escrow/KMS attestation for the fallback partner

If 14 days is permissible we can submit the evidence package by next Tuesday.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Manager, Customer Security
Redwood Inference
Attachment: subprocessor_roster_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: retirement-impact-matrix.pdf (pdf)
From: Marie Lopez <marie.lopez@blueharbor.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurements@blueharbor.com
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 11:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Subprocessor continuity / upcoming retirements — initial ask

Vanessa —

Thanks for the heads up and the attachments. Procurement needs a 30-day formal notification for any subprocessor decommissioning that could affect production telemetry or log retention. Compliance will accept a 14-day window only if you provide an escrow attestation plus a documented technical rollback plan and traffic routing proof.

Can you confirm whether RedWood (sic) has an onshore fallback that can accept EU telemetry without changing retention controls? If so, please send the attestation + routing diagrams and we can expedite to a 14-day review.

Regards,
Marie Lopez
Head of Procurement 
BlueHarbor Analytics
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: Marie Lopez <marie.lopez@blueharbor.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Dec 2026 12:35:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Subprocessor continuity / upcoming retirements — initial ask

Folks — forwarding BlueHarbor's response. TL;DR: procurement wants 30 days; compliance MAY accept 14 days if we provide escrow attestation + rollback/routing proof and confirm onshore fallback for EU telemetry.

Kimberly — can you pull the escrow/KMS attestation we have for OnshoreCache and confirm whether it covers the tenants Marie referenced (EU-prod-01, EU-analytics)? If it doesn't, can we get a scoped attestation before EOD tomorrow?

Markus — can you draft a short technical routing diagram and a one-paragraph rollback plan for switching telemetry from EdgeSight -> OnshoreCache (failover), including expected RTO and data retention parity? Procurement will need this in the packet.

If we can get all evidence together within 24 hours I think Marie's team may accept the 14-day path and move faster.

Thanks —
V

Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 07:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Subprocessor continuity / upcoming retirements — initial ask

Vanessa / Markus —

I pulled the OnshoreCache attestation (attached) — it covers encryption at rest with CMK under customer KMS and explicitly supports ingestion for EU tenants listed as EU-prod-01 and EU-analytics. Caveat: the attestation includes an exception around debug logs retained for 7 days in the backup path — compliance flagged that as acceptable if retention parity is documented.

I've attached a signed PDF attestation and the SOW excerpt that maps the tenant IDs. I also noted the escrow contact who can provide code/infra escrow if procurement wants deeper guarantees.

Attachment: onshorecache_attestation_signed.pdf
Attachment: onshorecache_sow_excerpt.txt

Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: markus.klein@redwood.com <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: Marie Lopez <marie.lopez@blueharbor.com>, procurements@blueharbor.com
Date: Wed, 23 Dec 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Subprocessor continuity / upcoming retirements — initial ask

Marie / Vanessa / Team —

Attached is the routing diagram (PDF) and a concise rollback plan. Summary:
- Failover path: EdgeSight -> OnshoreCache (active-passive)
- Expected RTO: 3 minutes for telemetry ingestion switch; client SDK fallback already supported for 99% of calls
- Retention parity: OnshoreCache maintains same retention and redaction rules; debug backups flagged and handled under the attestation Kim provided

We recommend the 14-day accelerated review if BlueHarbor accepts the signed attestation + the rollback diagram. If procurement insists on 30 days we will submit the formal 30-day notice and follow the standard notification calendar.

Attachments: routing_diagram_onshorecache.pdf, rollback-plan-one-pager.docx

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference
